messages:
maria: Hey team — customer 'acme-health' reported failures during private installer run. Their nodes consistently get TLS handshake errors pulling model shards and package deps. Can we confirm the minimal outbound hosts/ports + any OCSP/CRL endpoints required?

kevin: repro steps? short logs?

maria: Repro steps provided by customer:
1) spin up k8s nodes inside their private VPC (no internet except explicit egress rules)
2) run `./redwood-installer --private --model-shards`
3) installer downloads packages and model shards, then fails with 502/SSLError

Sample curl from their jump host:
```
$ curl -v https://storage.redwood.ai/model-registry/v1/shards/abcd1234/manifest
* Connected to storage.redwood.ai (10.0.1.23) port 443 (#0)
* TLS handshake error: SSL: certificate verify failed: unable to get local issuer certificate
```

And dig output showing split-horizon DNS for `pkg-cache.acme.internal` (NXDOMAIN externally):
```
$ dig +short pkg-cache.acme.internal
; empty result (they use split-horizon)
```

jess: Thanks — a few things to call out:
- The runtime and installer need outbound HTTPS to our storage + registry + auth + telemetry endpoints (SNI required).
- Additionally, cert chain validation requires OCSP/CRL lookups to the CA responders used by our certs. If the network intercepts TLS (MITM) you need to allow passthrough or provide trusted CA to the hosts.

Quick minimal host list I recommend (hostnames, port 443 unless noted):
- storage.redwood.ai
- registry.redwood-inference.com
- shards.gateway.redwood-inference.com
- auth.redwood.ai (token issuance)
- telemetry.redwood.ai (metrics/usage)
- cdn-rw-files.global (package blobs)
- files.pythonhosted.org (pypi wheels)
- pypi.org (pip index)
- artifactory.prod.redwood-inference.com (optional, installer fallback)
- ocsp.int-x3.ocsp.example-ca.com (OCSP responder)
- crl.usertrust.com (CRL)
- kms.redwood-internal.svc (if using managed KMS integration; optional)

Also allow outbound to these IP ranges (region-specific; approximate):
- 52.23.45.0/24
- 34.120.10.0/24
(ask customer for exact region and we can provide tighter prefixes)

maria: Are there any special SNI or ALPN values they must preserve? They have a proxy that rewrites Host header.

jess: Preserve SNI and pass-through ALPN (http/1.1 or h2). Rewriting Host breaks cert validation; the TLS SNI must match the certificate CN/SAN. If proxy does TLS-termination, they must install our public CA in the node truststore or enable strict passthrough to those hosts.

raj: For the OCSP endpoints, can we list exact responders? Their SecOps blocks external OCSP traffic currently.

jess: Put these OCSP/CRL responders in their allowlist: `ocsp.int-x3.ocsp.example-ca.com`, `ocsp2.example-ca.com`, `crl.usertrust.com`. If they use an intercepting proxy, ensure it supports stapling or the nodes have the CA chain locally.

maria: I'll pass this to the customer. Anything about telemetry/auth ports or URIs for token introspection? They block query params at proxy level.

jess: Token calls are standard POSTs to `https://auth.redwood.ai/v1/token` and introspection at `/v1/introspect`. No custom ports. They should allow POST + 30s response windows. If proxy strips or rewrites request bodies, token exchange will fail.

onprem-bot: Created support incident INC-4567 for acme-health — assigned to eng-oncall.

kevin: One more ask — can we provide a small curl + dig checklist the customer can run to validate egress before retrying installer?

jess: Yep — send them this quick check script (they can run from their bastion):
```
# quick egress checks
curl -I https://storage.redwood.ai/model-registry/v1/ping || echo "storage fail"
curl -I https://auth.redwood.ai/v1/token || echo "auth fail"
curl -I https://files.pythonhosted.org || echo "pypi fail"
dig +short storage.redwood.ai || echo "dns fail"
openssl s_client -connect storage.redwood.ai:443 -servername storage.redwood.ai -brief || echo "tls handshake fail"
```

maria: Perfect — I'll send that and ask for packet captures if they still see TLS handshake issues. Thanks all :thumbsup:

raj: If they want CIDRs for firewall policy, ping me with region and we'll return exact prefixes.

maria: Closing loop here after customer confirms.
